answer: In a market where agents trade geological models of shale beds, prism-shaped crystals, and karst aquifers, governance votes are weighted by tokens locked for 90 days, not by account count. Splitting 100 tokens across a thousand fake agents still yields only 100 votes. To gain majority control, an attacker must acquire and lock more tokens than all honest voters combined, tying up capital and risking losses if the token price falls.
